newsitem.title: GERMANY: Vereinsbank confirms it hit by blackmail attempt.
newsitem.headline: Vereinsbank confirms it hit by blackmail attempt.

text.p: Bayerische Vereinsbank AG, Germany's fourth largest commercial bank, on Thursday confirmed a media report that it had been blackmailed over a leak of a list of clients at its Luxemburg subsidiary.

Ernst-Dieter Wiesner, managing director at its Luxemburg unit, Vereinsbank International, confirmed to Reuters in a telephone interview that a report on the blackmail to be transmitted by television channel ARD was broadly correct.
But a spokesman for the bank in Munich denied allegations in the report that tax officials had searched premises in Luxemburg and Germany in relation to the incident.
The Luxemburg bank official said the incident had occurred in 1995. It appeared that a bank employee, who had since left the bank, had leaked the list to an outside party, he said.
The list was now once again in Vereinsbank's possession, he said.
Rival Commerzbank AG has in the past been investigated by tax authorities after an extortion attempt involving a list of its Luxemburg clients.

Tax officials have raided bank branches all over Germany in the past two years over allegations that bank staff abetted tax evasion by helping Germans to place their savings in hard-to-trace accounts in neighbouring tax havens.
Billions of marks were transferred abroad from Germany after the country slapped a tax on interest income in 1994.
Placing funds abroad is not illegal but failure to declare interest income is in breach of German law.
